rationale: This is a mechanical first-difference of the archive's "Organic R&D Liability Coverage" (both legs simply differenced), and because DELTA of MA(xrd/at)/(lt/at) is dominated by year-over-year leverage changes rather than R&D, it is more likely to destroy the level signal's alpha than to repair its Fama-MacBeth slope.

It is largely a sign-flipped reassembly of the already-null "Debt-Funded Goodwill Margin Decay" with a maturity-share leg borrowed from "Patient Stable Brand Runway," and the triple product of non-negative ranks makes the interaction unidentified — firms with low goodwill and improving margins are scored low, which the hypothesis never justifies.

This is a one-variable substitution (dlc for lt) on the archive's "Liability-Burdened Ad Gross-Profit Strain," i.e., a cosmetic variant of an already-tested marginal signal rather than a new mechanism.

It swaps the goodwill leg of the near-null "Flexible-Financed R&D Exercise" for revenue growth already used in "Nondilutive R&D Revenue Conversion" and "Self-Financing R&D Commercialization," and the reinterpretation of liability-ratio volatility as "flexibility" is asserted rather than argued, leaving a three-way all-positive rank product with no clear economic direction.

Adding a gross-margin realization leg to the debt-retirement/R&D-trend pair is a substantive conditioning refinement with a coherent sign convention, though the debt-retirement leg is close to the well-known net-debt-financing anomaly and the prior version's significantly negative FF5 alpha argues the expected positive sign may be wrong.

The maturity-spread × identifiable-intangible-growth pairing is a genuinely new combination in this archive with a clean two-leg structure whose signed direction matches the hypothesis, though it is a recombination of legs from "Long-Maturity Organic Runway" and "Deleveraging Identifiable Intangible Build" and DELTA(intan−gdwl) is partly mechanical amortization noise.
